part: P5A Part 29 -- Expected Steady-State Growth Model
objective: Using the real HOT/COLD split ratio and known production growth rate, project bounded-HOT vs current-unbounded main-DB size growth.

inputs.daily_ingest_rows_source: docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p3_long_term_growth_model.json inputs_used -- a 14-day measured block_time window average, carried forward from P3 (MEDIUM confidence per that artifact's own disclosure: treating a 14-day average as representative steady-state is an assumption, not a long-term-verified rate)
inputs.bytes_per_row_source: Part 28 of THIS milestone -- a REAL PRAGMA dbstat measurement against live production transfer_index (2,182,950,912 bytes / 5,284,432 rows), superseding P3's earlier LOW-confidence analytical estimate (120-180 bytes/row, dbstat 'not safely obtainable' at that time). This is a genuine confidence upgrade this session.
inputs.cold_fraction_source: Part 14 frozen accounting (1,735,652 COLD / 5,223,038 total at high-water id 6648855)
inputs.pinned_rows_source: Part 14 / original P5A classification (creator_funders + wt_ops_v2 operator_entities + discovery-corpus signature pins)

current_architecture_unbounded_growth.description: Today, ALL transfer_index rows (HOT-eligible and COLD-eligible alike) live permanently in the single monolithic main DB. Main DB size grows without bound as ingest continues.
current_architecture_unbounded_growth.caveat: Assumes the 14-day measured daily ingest rate (171,796 rows/day) holds as a long-term steady-state average -- real growth could be higher (organic platform growth) or lower (rate is itself somewhat volatile per P3's disclosed 77,060-402,792 daily range).

proposed_architecture_bounded_hot_model.description: Post-P5B-cutover, only HOT-classified rows (90-day recency window UNION a pinned set) live in the main DB; COLD rows live in separate, append-only monthly segment files outside the main DB.
proposed_architecture_bounded_hot_model.hot_growth_characteristic: BOUNDED -- the recency-window component (90 days x daily rate) is a rolling window that does not grow over time (old rows exit HOT as new rows enter, net-zero at steady state); the pinned component grows only as NEW addresses get pinned (via creator_funders/wt_ops_v2/discovery-corpus criteria), which is a much slower, sub-linear growth relative to raw transaction ingest -- so total HOT size approaches a ceiling rather than growing unboundedly.
proposed_architecture_bounded_hot_model.cold_growth_characteristic: UNBOUNDED but OUTSIDE the main DB -- COLD accumulates in separate monthly .sqlite segment files (already proven to scale cleanly across 41 real segments in Part 27). This growth does not inflate main-DB size, main-DB query latency for HOT-scoped queries, or main-DB backup/VACUUM/WAL-checkpoint cost.
proposed_architecture_bounded_hot_model.cold_projection_caveat: COLD accumulation is spread across many small monthly files (Part 28 showed 41 real segments totaling only ~1.0 GB today, i.e. ~25 MB/segment average) rather than one growing monolith -- this is architecturally significant even though the RAW BYTE total is comparable to the unbounded model's growth, because per-file size stays small and bounded per month, and old segments can be moved to cheaper storage tiers independently without touching the main DB.

comparison_summary.main_db_growth_5yr_bounded_hot_gb: ~0 (HOT stabilizes near its 6.72 GB ceiling; no further main-DB growth from transfer_index specifically, modulo the slow-growing pinned-set contribution)
comparison_summary.key_benefit: The bounded-HOT model converts transfer_index from an UNBOUNDED main-DB liability into a BOUNDED ~6.7 GB steady-state cost, while total data volume (HOT+COLD combined) grows at essentially the same real rate either way -- the win is entirely architectural (where the growth lives, not how much data exists), consistent with Part 26's finding that this split doesn't reduce total work, it isolates hot-path query cost from cold-history volume.

confidence_disclosure.pinned_set_growth_rate_confidence: NOT MODELED -- assumed slow/sub-linear based on qualitative reasoning (pinning criteria require becoming a creator_funders/wt_ops_v2/discovery-corpus entity, a much rarer event than raw transaction ingest), not independently measured this session
confidence_disclosure.overall_model_confidence: MEDIUM -- real inputs where available (row bytes, HOT/COLD split ratio), with one inherited MEDIUM-confidence input (daily ingest rate) and one unmodeled assumption (pinned-set growth rate) disclosed rather than hidden
